title: 118 AI-generated signals, benchmarked against each sector's own ETF (not just the S&P)
author: Downtown_Extension_6
selftext:
Disclosure: my own project, paper-traded, not investment advice.



Most "my AI beats the market" posts compare to SPY and stop there. That bundles sector luck into what looks like skill. So I benchmarked every signal against its \*own\* sector's ETF, over the same trigger-to-current window.



\*\*Overall:\*\* 118 signals, +4.2% avg vs +0.6% for SPY → \*\*+3.6pp\*\*.



\*\*By sector, where the sample is actually usable (n≥13):\*\*



| Sector | N | Picks | Sector ETF | Delta |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Semiconductors | 22 | −1.0% | −5.8% | \*\*+4.8pp\*\* |

| Financials | 9 | +13.8% | +9.1% | +4.7pp |

| Technology | 23 | −0.3% | −3.6% | \*\*+3.3pp\*\* |

| Energy | 21 | +8.3% | +4.0% | +4.3pp |

| Utilities | 13 | +1.2% | −0.2% | +1.3pp |

| Healthcare | 14 | +7.7% | +10.4% | \*\*−2.8pp\*\* |



The two rows I find most interesting: \*\*Semis and Tech had negative raw returns but positive alpha.\*\* The picks lost money and still beat their sector — selection working even in a down tape. That's the opposite of Healthcare, which looked fine on raw return (+7.7%) but lagged XLV. Beta wearing a costume.



Honest caveats: win rate \~61%, single \~2-month regime, open paper positions marked to market. I'm not counting the sub-10-signal sectors (Consumer Disc shows +18pp on 4 signals — that's variance, not a result).
